chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Joining Wilbur De Paris: rehearsals and Atlantic records
summary: De Paris rehearsed twice a week for two months at Ryan's before the 1952 Atlantic recordings.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Let's see, now. We move up to Wilbur De Paris. De Paris was actually from Indiana. But you joined him, you played with him for a couple of years, and you recorded with him -- you made some dates with Atlantic Records in 1952. How did you join Wilbur De Paris, and...
What did Wilbur De Paris ask you to do as a drummer?

Just play like I felt, play relaxed drums, keep the beat, listen to the band... He rehearsed that band twice a week for two months before he went in Jimmy Ryan's. Twice a week he rehearsed the band. We mostly rehearsed right down there in Jimmy Ryan's on the bandstand. There was never nobody in there, you know... The time we'd have
rehearsals, it would be around two or three o'clock in the afternoon. It would be about two hours. We'd sit around sometimes until four or 4:30. He had Don Rd on piano, Omer Simeon on clarinet.
Eddie Gibbs was a banjo player.
Tell us a little about him. He's not very well known. Was he an older musician, around the age of de Paris? Or was he a young...?
Yeah, he was older than us.

Harold Jackson, the bass player. We're (?), okay. Now, de Paris in this recording, New Orleans Jazz on Atlantic Records, this is Atlantic 141, there are interesting selections here. There's a "Prelude In C-Sharp Minor" which is arranged by Wilbur de Paris. Was that a popular number that... Was that number popular with the de Paris band, and was it popular with people who enjoyed listening to the band?
Well, I think that was one of Wilbur's numbers. He liked that number very much. "C-Sharp Minor?"
